model_result.answer_summary: Atomic abundance of 235U in natural uranium = 2/301 ≈ 0.6644518... % of atoms, reported as 0.664 % (3 significant figures). Derived from 235.04·x + 238.05·(1−x) = 238.03, where 235.04 and 238.05 are the isotopic masses given in problem 4.1 (Q4-1, theory_problem.pdf p.37) and 238.03 is the atomic weight of uranium printed in the official IChO 2026 periodic table (theory_problem.pdf, page header G1-5).
assumptions: Natural uranium is a two-component isotopic mixture of 235U and 238U only (stated in problem 4.1).
Isotopic masses m(235U)=235.04 a.u. and m(238U)=238.05 a.u. are exact stipulated constants as printed in the problem (Q4-1, theory_problem.pdf source page 37).

The average atomic weight of natural uranium A(U)=238.03 is the value printed under 'U' in the official 'Periodic Table of Elements' included in theory_problem.pdf (page header G1-5, PDF page 5); it is a stipulated tabulated constant of the examination booklet, treated as exact as printed.
Mean isotopic mass of the mixture equals the abundance-weighted sum of the isotopic masses (standard two-component mixing law implicit in the problem).
Reporting is at three significant figures per the target's answer-blind reporting policy (the problem itself specifies no precision).
